title: hZCCL: Accelerating Collective Communication with Co-Designed Homomorphic Compression
problem: Network bandwidth cannot keep up with computing capabilities, making collective communication efficiency critical. Traditional decompression-operation-compression (DOC) workflows are expensive and expose poor performance.
motivation: Efficient collective communication is essential for exa-scale distributed and parallel applications as computing capabilities grow faster than network bandwidth.
method: hZCCL enables operations to be performed directly on homomorphically compressed data, eliminating expensive decompression-operation-compression cycles. The system includes a lightweight compressor optimized for multi-core CPUs and a homomorphic compressor with runtime heuristics that dynamically select efficient compression pipelines for reducing DOC handling costs.
key_novelty: Performing collective communication operations directly on homomorphically compressed data rather than requiring decompression before computation.
contributions: Homomorphic compression-communication co-design framework enabling operations on compressed data
Lightweight compressor optimized for multi-core CPU platforms achieving up to 379.08 GB/s throughput
Homomorphic compressor with runtime heuristics for dynamic compression pipeline selection
Up to 2.12x and 6.77x speedups on collective operations in single and multi-thread modes

metrics.speedup: up to 2.12x and 6.77x vs MPI collectives; up to 36.53x vs conventional DOC workflow

primary_theme: Homomorphic compression for efficient collective communication
